why: read_until/read_until_regex promise to close only if MORE than max_bytes were read without the delimiter. why: _find_read_pos is a linear search over the whole buffer. Called per chunk, a delimited read over n bytes costs O(n^2/chunk) instead of O(n): a large read_until without max_bytes burns CPU quadratically. Results are the same.
note_must_say: _read_to_buffer_loop calls the linear _find_read_pos on every read (doubling guard gone), making large delimited reads quadratic.

what: The header sanity check regex only matches the two-byte sequence CRLF, not a lone CR or a lone LF.
why: write_headers relies on this to reject header injection. HTTPHeaders.__setitem__ does no validation, and this same package accepts bare LF as a line terminator on input (parse_line), so a header value containing a bare \n coming from application or user data now reaches the wire: response splitting / header injection.
note_must_say: CR_OR_LF_RE matches only the sequence CRLF, so a header value with a bare CR or LF passes the check (header injection).

what: The active-requests dictionary became a class attribute shared by every SimpleAsyncHTTPClient instance instead of per-instance state.
why: max_clients is documented per client, and clients exist per IOLoop or with force_instance=True.
